findings.summary: PreflightOptions.repoRoot is non-functional and its local binding is dead: runPreflight computes `const repoRoot = opts.repoRoot ?? resolve(contractRoot, "..")` at line 204 but never reads it, because artifact.ref / working_directory / relative command paths are resolved by resolveAgainstRepoRoot and resolveExecutable against the module-level REPO_ROOT constant derived from import.meta.url. An injected contractRoot/repoRoot therefore relocates only applications.json and the declaration file, while existence checks silently still resolve against the real repository root. No current caller passes these options, so no shipped behavior or acceptance assertion is wrong today; the risk is a future harness validating paths it did not intend to.

The compatibility probe added to the pre-existing E2E suite widens the skip surface with a single misleading message. loopEngineRegistryCompatible() returns false for at least four distinct causes -- bun unresolvable, /data/worktrees/loop-engine-v1build/dist/lib/model-registry.js absent, the 10s execFileSync timeout, and any import error unrelated to selector `route` -- but B1/B2 are then skipped with a message asserting specifically that the external build cannot load chain selectors without `route`. If that external build is ever relocated or restructured, two real end-to-end tests degrade to an explicit-but-wrongly-explained skip. This also sits against the in-file prohibition at test/a10b-convergence.test.ts:277 ("不得改回续投门或 skip/删用例"), which the change neither removes nor amends, though the skip does follow the file's established missing-dependency discipline (line 16) rather than a silent pass. Not blocking: the branch is honest, self-restoring, documented in deploy/README.md sec 8, and touches nothing in the C1 preflight runner or its tests.

The recorded acceptance run does not exercise the skip branch that the change was made to add. The implement verification record reports `npm test` (unscoped) with {failed:0, passed:793, total:793} and zero skips, while the prior attempt recorded {failed:2, passed:791, total:793} over the same test count -- so at verification time MODEL_REGISTRY_COMPATIBLE evaluated true and B1/B2 ran and passed rather than skipping. The dd-acceptance gate is therefore genuinely green on the unscoped command (resolving the blockers from rf-e156b85b and rc-1f139fd7), but the new compatibility-probe path has no recorded green run behind it. I cannot execute tests, so this is read from the committed record, not reproduced.

Provenance metadata is internally inconsistent, as it was in attempt 1: the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit=821f63744c2743e96719f63632c8c86ae17a6ce5, while the dispatch attempt context states the product commit (work_head_commit) is 9e38abf8f5785a5f2367388c03bac55339803249 -- which it also gives as implementation_subject_commit. Non-blocking and consistent with a metadata-only seal stacked on the product commit, but the two records do not name the same SHA, and the Continuous review asserted these agree.

Review-coverage limitation, not a defect in the change: as a read-only reviewer restricted to file inspection (shell access is confined to the session workdir) I did not execute the prescribed mechanical check `git diff --exit-code 9e38abf8 07780340 -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'`, and I claim no git or shell execution. By direct inspection of the worktree I observed the complete C1 product implementation intact -- deploy/ contract, schema, both declarations, src/preflight.ts, src/preflight-entry.ts, test/c1-preflight.test.ts, all four fixtures, package.json preflight scripts -- and found no product file bearing evidence of alteration by the review materialization seal. The deterministic verdict seal remains the authoritative independent check of the actual Git HEAD.
